_**Agent**_

Looking at your code, I've identified why assistant responses aren't showing up: the `MessagesWithNotesSaving` component is defined in the `mindmap-bottom-menu.tsx` file but never actually rendered in the UI.

The component is properly defined:

```jsx
const MessagesWithNotesSaving = ({messages}: {messages: AISdkMessage[]}) => {
  const {addNoteFromMessage} = useSessionNotes()
  const convertedMessages = messages.map((msg) => convertAiSdkMessage(msg))
  return <MindMapMessages messages={convertedMessages} onSaveAsNote={addNoteFromMessage} />
}
```

But it's not included in the component's JSX output anywhere. To fix this, you need to add the component to your UI, likely within the form or near the input area.

Add this inside your JSX in `MindMapBottomMenu`, possibly right before the form element or after the error message display:

```jsx
{messages.length > 0 && <MessagesWithNotesSaving messages={messages} />}
```

This will render the messages component whenever there are messages to display, showing both user and assistant responses.

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "\n\nexport const OracleCommandMenu = ({\n  commandMenuOpen,\n  activeCommand,\n  commands,\n  handleCommandSelect,\n  inputValue = '',\n  setInputValue,\n  handleKeyDown,\n}: OracleCommandMenuProps) =\u003e {\n  // Internal state for filtered commands\n  const [filteredCommands, setFilteredCommands] = useState\u003cReadonlyArray\u003cCommandItem\u003e\u003e(commands)\n\n  // Filter commands based on input value\n  useEffect(() =\u003e {\n    if (inputValue.startsWith('/')) {\n      const searchTerm = inputValue.slice(1).toLowerCase()\n      const filtered = commands.filter(\n        (command) =\u003e\n          (command.name?.toLowerCase() || '').includes(searchTerm) ||\n          (command.label?.toLowerCase() || '').includes(searchTerm) ||\n          command.id.toLowerCase().includes(searchTerm) ||\n          (command.prefix?.toLowerCase() || '').includes(searchTerm)\n      )\n      setFilteredCommands(filtered)\n    } else {\n      setFilteredCommands(commands)\n    }\n  }, [inputValue, commands])\n\n  // Function to handle command selection\n  const handleItemSelect = (command: CommandItem) =\u003e {\n    // Clear input when selecting a command\n    if (setInputValue) {\n      setInputValue('')\n    }\n\n    // Use the original ID format if possible for display purposes\n    // This ensures commands like \"Search\" retain their capitalization instead of \"search\"\n    const displayId = command.label || command.name || command.id\n\n    console.log('🚀 ~ handleItemSelect ~ displayId:', displayId)\n\n    // Call the parent handler with the proper ID\n    handleCommandSelect(displayId)\n  }\n\n  // Determine if we should show the input-specific style\n  const useInputStyle = Boolean(inputValue \u0026\u0026 inputValue.startsWith('/'))\n\n  // Skip rendering if not open or if a command is already active\n  if (!commandMenuOpen || activeCommand) {\n    return null\n  }",
